profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest speedup (0.17234) and highest eval latency (19.544 ms) in the round; fp16 2048x2048 last-axis case with ncols=2048 > DENSE_MAX_COLS=1700, so it is the representative of the large-ncols fp32 atomic path.
Second-lowest speedup regime (0.29690, 2.887 ms) and the representative of the destination-owned compare kernel (ncols=1024 <= 1700), which is the path the frozen hypothesis targeted.
Smallest-shape control (128x128 fp16, 0.10237 ms, speedup 1.2960) on the same owner path, used to separate per-call launch/host cost from device cost.

findings.label: Large-ncols atomic path saturates the MTE3 pipe with single-element atomic stores at ~4.5 ns per 2-byte transaction
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary row for _scatter_add_lastdim_kernel; aiv_mte3_time_us=18916.4, aiv_scalar_ratio=0.136; measured_invocations=100
findings.inference: The 2048x2048 case runs one kernel (_scatter_add_lastdim_kernel) with 4096 programmed blocks (2048 rows x 2 column blocks of 1024) and one tl.atomic_add per source element, i.e. 4.19M atomic updates. MTE3 is busy 97.5% of the 19.39 ms kernel while MTE2 is 0.8% and VEC is 0.02%, so 18.9 ms of MTE3 activity accounts for ~4.5 ns per single-element 2-byte atomic store. The payload moved in that time is only ~8.4 MB, and the two contiguous _copy_kernel tasks in the same call move 16 MiB in ~20-29 us each; therefore the limiter is the per-transaction cost of the lowered per-lane atomic store, not HBM bytes and not arithmetic. This is consistent with the already-recorded lowering of data-dependent atomics to a per-lane scf.for of single-element stores. The fp32 staging buffer and its two copies cost only ~40 us out of 19.54 ms of eval latency, so they are not a target.

findings.label: Destination-owned compare kernel is vector-pipe bound with a low retired-lane rate per vector-pipe second
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary rows for variant timing-1; per-invocation duration is stable at 2873.8-2881.0 us over 100 measured invocations
findings.inference: The case is a single launch (no copy kernels appear in the report) of 4096 blocks = 1024 rows x 4 destination blocks of 256, with CHUNK=32, so the dense compare fan-out is rows*ncols*ncols = 1.07e9 compare/select lanes. VEC is busy 2651.6 us of a 2877.1 us kernel (92.2%) while MTE3 is 0.5% and MTE2 15.7%, so this regime is vector-pipe bound. Retiring 1.07e9 compare lanes in 2651 us is only ~4e11 lanes/s aggregate, i.e. a few lanes per cycle per AIV core for a 36-40 core part, which is far below fp32 vector width. That pattern points to per-lane instruction overhead in the generated inner loop (materializing a [CHUNK, BLOCK] fp32 tile by broadcasting val, then reducing over the non-contiguous axis 0) rather than to raw lane throughput, and it explains why the same frozen case remains 3.4x slower than the 0.857 ms reference. Confidence is medium, not high: the artifact does not state how aiv_vec_time/aiv_total_cycles are aggregated across cores, so the per-cycle figure is approximate, and no instruction-level artifact exists for this round to name the dominating vector op.

findings.label: 128x128 case is dominated by per-call host/launch time, not by the 15 us device kernel
findings.backend_detail: execution-trace start-time deltas; op_summary shows block_num=128 and aiv_vec_ratio=0.537, aiv_scalar_ratio=0.562 on a 15 us kernel
findings.inference: In the execution timeline each _scatter_add_owner_kernel device task lasts 14.5-16.2 us, but successive kernel starts on the same stream are ~125-163 us apart (e.g. ts 1792689804788010.677 -> 1792689804788173.480 = 162.8 us), and the authoritative eval walltime for the same case is 102.4 us (from get_profile_context). The device kernel therefore accounts for only a small fraction of the measured call; the rest is per-call host dispatch and buffer allocation. The gaps observed under the profiler exceed the eval-derived difference because collection adds its own overhead, so no exact host/device split is claimed. Because this case already reports speedup 1.2960 and reference side is also launch dominated, host-path savings here move the headline metric only weakly.

performance_interpretation: The frozen hypothesis is SUPPORTED by this round's evidence for the regimes it targeted, and it also predicted correctly where it would not apply. Eval geo_mean rose 0.37028 -> 0.41522 (+12.14%) and the gains are concentrated exactly where the plan predicted: the destination-owned 1024x1024 cases fell 23.2%/23.2%/18.9% (3.757->2.887 ms, 3.758->2.888 ms, 3.538->2.868 ms) and the 128x128 cases fell 10.6%/3.1%/1.5%, consistent with removing one full-width boolean/mask term from the owner loop; the 2048x2048 cases moved by at most 0.23% because ncols=2048 never enters the owner path, so the crossover edit was a no-op there. The round therefore did not address its dominant loss: three cases at speedup ~0.172 account for most of the geo_mean deficit, and profile evidence attributes them to a ~4.5 ns per-transaction atomic-store cost (MTE3 97.5% busy) rather than to bandwidth, which no BLOCK or crossover tuning removes. In the owner regime the remaining 3.4x gap to reference is vector-pipe work: the dense fan-out is rows*ncols^2 lanes and the measured retired-lane rate is only a few lanes/cycle/core, so the inner-loop formulation, not the mask term any more, is the plausible lever. The 128x128 regime is launch bound (~15 us device inside a 102.4 us call) and is already faster than reference. Consequently the bound is mixed and workload-scoped: memory/transaction granularity for ncols>=2048, compute (vector pipe) for ncols<=1024 in the timing set, and launch/host for 128x128. No quantitative Roofline is claimed: the artifact gives pipe busy ratios and transaction counts, not physical HBM bytes against a calibrated bandwidth ceiling.

next_experiment.action_description: In _scatter_add_owner_kernel only, restructure the dense compare/reduce to reduce along the contiguous (last) axis with identical algebra: build the hit tile as [BLOCK, CHUNK] (dst[:, None] == idx[None, :]) and accumulate acc += tl.sum(tl.where(hit, val[None, :], 0.0), axis=1) instead of the current [CHUNK, BLOCK] tile reduced with axis=0; keep fp32 accumulation, keep the idx load with other=-1, keep the atomic kernel, the copy kernels and the host fast path untouched. In the same micro-probe, measure single-launch device time for ncols=1024 and ncols=2048 and re-derive DENSE_MAX_COLS from those measured owner-vs-atomic times instead of reusing the current 1700 constant.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Falsifiable test of the vector-overhead mechanism: if the non-contiguous axis-0 reduction is what suppresses the lane rate, the 1024x1024 owner device time should fall below the measured 2877 us with VEC time dropping and scalar/MTE2 roughly unchanged, lifting each of the three 1024x1024 cases and the headline geo_mean as (old/new)^(3/9). If the probe shows the 2048x2048 owner time below the measured 19.39 ms atomic time, raising the crossover adds up to ~1.7x geo_mean headroom on the three 2048x2048 cases; if it does not, the atomic path must be kept for ncols=2048. If neither VEC time nor total time moves, the axis-0 reduction hypothesis is falsified and the next candidate is offloading the reduction to the idle Cube unit (cube_utilization_pct is 0 in all rows) for the fp16/bf16 cases.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Precision: the rearrangement changes the intra-chunk summation order, and bf16 duplicate-index accumulation is the known historical failure area for this operator, so re-run the duplicate-index/grouped-index semantic checks and the numerical check of all 9 frozen timing inputs against the oracle before any formal eval; keep fp32 accumulate and revert the rearrangement if any tolerance fails. Resources: the [BLOCK, CHUNK] fp32 tile is the same 32 KB as today, so no new UB pressure is expected at CHUNK=32; if CHUNK is raised, verify the compiled UB requirement rather than assuming it fits in the 192 KB limit. Rollback is a single-function revert to the current inner loop, since the atomic path, host fast path and threshold logic are unchanged and no other case can regress.
success_criteria: Full KGS eval PASSED on all 9 correctness and 9 timing workloads with the frozen tolerances unchanged.
Independent semantic gate passes (18 items) plus all 9 frozen timing-input numerical checks, including duplicate-index, non-contiguous and negative-dim cases.
1024x1024 owner device time falls below the measured 2877 us (eval latency below 2.887 ms) with VEC ratio still high but total duration lower.
No regression on the 2048x2048 cases, which must stay at or below the measured 19.54 ms eval / 19.39 ms device atomic time unless the probe proves the owner path is faster there.
No regression on the 128x128 cases (<= 0.1024 ms) and headline geo_mean > 0.41522.
